text.tspan: Every subject has the same five tokens
concern names the data, never a mechanism or a consumer
version is per concern: a breaking change is a new tree, so old and new run side by side
id is the entity the traffic is about
class is the nature of the traffic, which is where retention, trust and access divide
event is the message's type, so nothing has to open the body to route on it

g.text: One namespace per concern. Trees are disjoint, so versions move independently: conv is v2, agent and approval are v1

text.tspan: The subject carries the taxonomy, and that is structural rather than stylistic: NATS routes, filters, retains and authorises on subjects only, never on payloads. A type buried in the body can be received and discarded, nothing more. So the type is stated exactly once, and where it is a routing axis it is the subject's last token and the body does not repeat it.

The class token is where policy divides. Telemetry is publish-only and nothing acts on it, so the worst case of a bogus publish is a wrong pixel; the change stream is the system's truth, so reading it is reading state and writing it is acting. Keeping them in separate tokens is what lets a deployment grade the two differently.

Evolution is add-only within a version: producers may only add new events, fields and values, and every consumer must tolerate what it does not recognise. That is why a fold subscribes to a whole class and never to a list of leaves: a wildcard subscriber tolerates a new event type, while a leaf-list subscriber is silently blind to it, and on the change stream blind means wrong state with no error.
One boundary is contract rather than configuration: streams capture events only, never a requests subject.

Nothing on the wire enforces any of this, and there is no negotiation and no capability handshake. The system works because participants conform, which is why an independent agent like claude-sdk-cli can join by publishing the right subjects and nothing has to be told about it.
Colours: green = the committal record, cyan = observation, orange = requests, purple = the naming rule, gold = capture, red = the boundary that must not be crossed.
the conversation: what was said, and what changed it
who is serving conversations, and where
the agent host: publishes what the agent does, answers what is asked of its world
a separate agent, written before any of this,
taking part by publishing the same subjects
folds the trees into state and serves the clients
the committal change stream: the record itself
who is serving this conversation, now
the in-progress message, chunk by chunk
flat on purpose: the type rides in the body,
because these shapes share every routing and retention rule
is a process up, and still promising to be
instances in a world share a queue group,
the pending ask's own pulse, about every 15s

g.text: publishes its world's ready and pulse
publishes its own conversations; towerd folds them beside the rest
folds every event class; subscribes to a whole class, never a set of leaves
one WebSocket, all of it already folded
sends the requests a user causes: say, cancel, chdir, service, drain, the approval answer
a request is answered by whoever holds the conversation, or by one instance in the world
captured, and replayed to rebuild state
never captured: a stream over a requests subject acknowledges the publish and becomes a second responder, racing the real reply
